message: Pre-existing, non-blocking hardening gap: if an update install handoff fails after Buddy has stopped the embedded backend but before application shutdown begins, the current app can remain open without restarting that backend. Normal macOS installer-launch failures occur before backend shutdown, most later installer failures are handled on the next launch, and the narrow Windows inconsistency is exceptional; this should not block the current updater PR. A future bounded fix may restart the previously running backend only when the install attempt fails while the application is not quitting.

Goal: let Buddy's agent control the exact Buddy-owned visible Electron browser guest, sharing page, cookies, and navigation with the user; an external browser/session is not desired. T3 Code's original PR chose this shared-session model. Its historical spike found Playwright connectOverCDP exposed the Electron host renderer but not its <webview> guest as a Playwright Page; that does not prove all reusable packages fail. T3 currently reuses playwright-core 1.60's injected runtime for locator semantics and Effect's MCP server, while owning CDP input, snapshots, and desktop/session routing. agent-browser is the best candidate found for a first Buddy spike: its Electron guide documents raw-CDP <webview> target selection plus snapshot/click/fill/screenshot, and it exposes a stdio MCP server via `agent-browser mcp`. Its npm package distributes a CLI/native executable, not an importable TypeScript SDK; integrating it through Buddy's existing local MCP support would add a helper process but no second browser. Buddy would need to provide a CDP endpoint, bind the right guest tab/session, and manage endpoint access and lifecycle. Python browser-use and TypeScript Browser Use Pi support existing Chrome CDP sessions, but Electron <webview> compatibility was not verified. If an in-process TypeScript API is required, evaluate puppeteer-core's webview-target support instead, with Buddy-owned tool wrappers. Before choosing, test the actual Buddy guest on macOS and Windows for same-session state, snapshots, click, fill, hidden tabs, and focus. No Buddy integration or live browser test was performed in this exploration.
